newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan asks banks to halt loan rescheduling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan asks banks to halt loan rescheduling.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has told banks and financial institutions to stop rescheduling loans until after elections set for February 3, central bank sources said on Tuesday.

They said a circular dated December 6 also asked commercial banks and financial institutions to submit lists by December 11 of individuals and firms that have defaulted on loan repayments or have had their loans written off since December 31, 1985.
The circular defined default as non-payment of a loan or interest payment for 364 days from the due date.
Bankers said the halt to rescheduling would have little impact on the overall corporate sector as the December-January period was usually a lean period for fresh advances.
"Most credit lines in these two months are earmarked for commodity operations and banks usually do not issue fresh loans or reschedule old ones during these months," said one banker.
The banker, who asked not to be named, said his bank had already submitted details of loan defaults and write-offs as requested by the SBP.

Analyst Aliya Ehmar of ING Baring Securities said officials of the Election Commission, SBP, and the state-run Banking Council of Pakistan had met last week to discuss how loan defaulters could be barred from contesting elections.
President Farooq Leghari issued an ordinance on Thursday stipulating that candidates would have to declare that they were not loan defaulters or tax evaders.

It said candidates could be barred from standing, and winning candidates could be dismissed, if found to have given false or incorrect information. In such cases they could be jailed for five years and fined 100,000 rupees ($2,500).

Leghari dismissed prime minister Benazir Bhutto on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, and dissolved the National Assembly on November 5. He named a caretaker government under Meraj Khalid to supervise elections.
